name: r3loop
description: Loop architecture for design ops. AI-orchestrated since 2022.

steps.name: Diagnose
steps.purpose: Find the real problem before designing anything
steps.ai_role: Pattern-match pain against known r3loop failure modes; generate interview templates; analyze workflow audits; identify bottlenecks with hypothesized impact
steps.human_role: Conduct interviews; approve audit scope; sign off on root-cause; prioritize bottlenecks
steps.decision_gate: Can I describe the operational problem in one sentence with a concrete time-cost number?

steps.name: Map
steps.ai_role: Classify requests from raw data; detect seasonality; calculate volume per stakeholder; identify request taxonomy
steps.human_role: Validate classification taxonomy; make accept/reject/defer decisions; approve mapping output
steps.decision_gate: Can a new request be classified at intake within 30 seconds, by anyone?

steps.name: Standardize
steps.ai_role: Generate brief templates per category; codify Definition of Ready; build quality checklists; create AI brief assistant prompts; score brief quality at submission
steps.human_role: Define quality standards; decide exceptions; approve template language; train team on usage
steps.decision_gate: Can a junior team member fill a brief WITHOUT asking the lead designer questions?

steps.name: Build
steps.purpose: Create what ships, against the standards
steps.ai_role: Generate v1 deliverables; apply brand constraints automatically; suggest variants; auto-check against quality checklist
steps.human_role: Senior execution refinement; strategic direction; taste decisions; approval per artifact type
steps.decision_gate: Can a developer/team implement this without asking a single question?

steps.name: Govern
steps.ai_role: Log decisions in structured format; route change requests; track decision velocity; flag stalled decisions
steps.human_role: Define ownership map; approve escalation paths; resolve conflicts when AI escalates
steps.decision_gate: For any artifact, can I name (a) who approved it, (b) when, (c) what the rationale was?

steps.name: Ship
steps.purpose: Deliver with quality gates, not hope
steps.ai_role: Run quality checklist automatically; generate handoff docs; pre-flight checks; compare deliverable to brief
steps.human_role: Final sign-off; edge case judgment; stakeholder communication around ship
steps.decision_gate: Did the deliverable match the brief AND pass quality checklist AND get sign-off?

steps.name: Measure
steps.ai_role: Aggregate metrics; generate KPI reports; detect anomalies; correlate metric movements with system changes
steps.human_role: Define what to measure; review reports + ask 'so what?'; communicate insights; decide when to investigate
steps.decision_gate: Can I show 3 measurable improvements vs baseline within 60 days?

steps.name: Iterate
steps.purpose: Keep the system alive, not frozen
steps.ai_role: Analyze metric trends; flag degradation; propose process changes with predicted impact; detect drift patterns
steps.human_role: Approve process changes; lead retrospectives; decide evolve vs maintain; sign off on system updates
steps.decision_gate: Can I take a 2-week vacation without the system breaking?

prompts.title: The 5-second test
prompts.agent_prompt:
You're a buyer arriving at a B2B service page. You see this hero block:
H1: '{{hero_h1}}'
Tagline: '{{tagline}}'
Sub: '{{sub_line}}'

Without scrolling, answer in 5 seconds: WHO is this person/company? WHO is it for? WHAT makes it different? If any answer is 'unclear' or 'need more context', flag the failed element. Return JSON: { who, target, differentiator, failed_elements[], pass: bool }
prompts.pass_criteria: All 3 questions answered concretely; no failed_elements

prompts.title: Tagline-H1 redundancy audit
prompts.agent_prompt:
Compare these two strings semantically. Are they making the same claim or distinct claims?
Tagline: '{{tagline}}'
H1: '{{h1}}'

Return: { redundancy_score: 0-1, recommendation: 'split'|'merge'|'keep', proposed_split: { identity_line, claim_line } if redundancy_score > 0.6 }
prompts.pass_criteria: redundancy_score < 0.4 OR explicit reason to keep similar

prompts.title: Audience qualifier visibility
prompts.pass_criteria: Either H1 is specific OR audience chips are visible

prompts.title: Mobile typography stress test
prompts.agent_prompt:
Simulate rendering H1 at 48px on 375px viewport. Word-break analysis:
Desktop: '{{h1_desktop}}'
Mobile: '{{h1_mobile}}'

Identify: words wider than 311px (375 - 64 padding), mid-word break risks, line wrap awkwardness.

Return: { word_break_detected: bool, problematic_words[], recommended_breaks: <inserted br tags>, recommended_font_size, recommended_leading }
prompts.pass_criteria: No word breaks mid-word; no orphan single-word lines; readable at 375px

prompts.title: Three-word category test
prompts.agent_prompt:
Compress this description into MAXIMUM 3 words that name your category:
'{{how_you_describe_what_you_do}}'

Examples of strong 3-word categories: 'Design ops methodology', 'Brand operating system', 'AI loop architecture'.

If you can't compress to 3 words, the category isn't named yet. Generate 5 candidate 3-word phrases. Score each by: specificity, ownability, memorability.

Return: { current_word_count, can_compress: bool, candidates: [{ phrase, scores }], recommended: <best phrase> }

_notes: First 5 of 50 prompts converted to JSON. Remaining 45 will be added in subsequent commits — same schema structure. Each prompt becomes a self-contained agent execution unit. Loadable into Next.js runtime via import or fetch.
